title: Core Security Domain 1: General Security Concepts, Zero Trust & PKI (12%)
overview: Covers Security Controls, CIA Triad, Zero Trust planes, Deception tech, and Cryptography/PKI fundamentals.
art: CIA TRIAD + AAA + NON-REPUDIATION (?1)        ZERO TRUST ARCHITECTURE (?2)
+ Non-Repudiation (Digital Signatures)       [ Subject ] ─►[ PEP ] ─► [ Enterprise Resource ]
Symmetric (AES-256: Fast, Same Key) vs Asymmetric (RSA/ECC: Public + Private Keys)
[ Root CA ] ──signs──► [ Intermediate CA ] ──signs──► [ Server Cert (X.509 / TLS) ]

1.label: Security Controls, CIA Triad & Non-Repudiation
1.what: Core principles of protecting information and classifying safeguards by how they are implemented and what function they serve.
1.exam_facts: CIA Triad: Confidentiality (Encryption, ACLs), Integrity (SHA-256 Hashing, HMAC), Availability (RAID, Redundancy, Backups). Non-Repudiation: Proves a sender cannot deny sending a message (achieved via Digital Signatures = Hash encrypted with Sender's Private Key). Control Categories: Technical (firewalls, MFA), Managerial (policies, risk assessments), Operational (security guards, awareness training), Physical (bollards, mantraps/access control vestibules). Control Types: Preventive (stops attack), Detective (alerts/logs), Corrective (restores system), Deterrent (warning signs), Compensating (alternative control), Directive (policies/SOPs).
1.troubleshoot: Exam Trap: Security exams frequently ask you to classify a control by BOTH category and type—for example, a firewall rule is Technical/Preventive, while a CCTV camera is Physical/Detective (and Deterrent).

2.label: Zero Trust Architecture & Deception Technologies
2.what: Replaces implicit trust based on physical/network location ('inside the LAN = safe') with continuous verification of identity, device posture, and least privilege.
2.exam_facts: Control Plane: Policy Engine (PE - makes grant/deny decision using threat intel & context) + Policy Administrator (PA - generates session token/credentials). Data Plane: Policy Enforcement Point (PEP - gateway/proxy that actually connects/blocks the user to the resource). Deception Tech: Honeypot (single decoy system), Honeynet (network of decoys), Honeyfile (fake sensitive file with tracking alert), Honeytoken (fake API key/credential planted to catch intruders early).
2.troubleshoot: Adaptive Identity dynamically adjusts access requirements—for example, prompting for MFA if a user logs in from an unrecognized IP or unmanaged device.

3.label: Symmetric vs. Asymmetric Encryption & Hashing
3.what: Cryptographic methods for protecting data at rest and in transit, verifying file integrity, and exchanging keys securely.
3.exam_facts: Symmetric (Same key encrypts & decrypts—fast for bulk data, hard to share keys safely): AES-128/256, ChaCha20 (Deprecated/weak: DES, 3DES, RC4). Asymmetric (Public key encrypts, Private key decrypts—slow, solves key exchange): RSA, ECC (Elliptic Curve—stronger with smaller keys, great for mobile/IoT), Diffie-Hellman / ECDHE (key exchange with Perfect Forward Secrecy). Hashing (One-way fixed-length digest, NO decryption): SHA-256, SHA-3 (Deprecated/broken: MD5, SHA-1). Salting adds random data before hashing passwords to defeat Rainbow Tables; Key Stretching (bcrypt, Argon2, PBKDF2) slows down brute-force attacks.
3.troubleshoot: In TLS/HTTPS, Asymmetric crypto (ECDHE/RSA) is ONLY used during the initial handshake to safely agree on a shared Symmetric session key (AES), which then encrypts the actual data stream at high speed!

4.label: Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), Certificates & TPM/HSM
4.what: The hardware, software, policies, and Certificate Authorities (CAs) that issue, validate, and revoke digital certificates binding public keys to identities.
4.exam_facts: X.509 Certificate fields: Subject, Issuer, Public Key, Validity Period, Serial Number, Signature. Wildcard Cert (*.domain.com) secures all first-level subdomains. CSR (Certificate Signing Request) is generated with your public key and sent to the CA. Revocation: CRL (Certificate Revocation List - downloaded list, slower) vs OCSP (Online Certificate Status Protocol - real-time query) & OCSP Stapling (web server attaches timestamped OCSP response to speed up TLS). Hardware Crypto: TPM (Trusted Platform Module - motherboard chip storing BitLocker/boot keys) vs HSM (Hardware Security Module - dedicated enterprise appliance/card for high-speed CA/key management).
4.troubleshoot: If a browser throws `ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID` on an internal web app, the client machine doesn't trust your internal Enterprise Root CA—deploy the Root CA cert via Group Policy (GPO) or MDM.
